name: MKW41Z512VHT4R
title: 2.4 GHz Bluetooth Low Energy, IEEE 802.15.4 and generic FSK wireless microcontroller, Cortex-M0+
summary: A single-chip 2.4 GHz radio and 48 MHz Arm Cortex-M0+ microcontroller with up to 512 KB of flash and 128 KB of SRAM in a 7 x 7 mm 48-pin laminate QFN. The transceiver covers 2.360 GHz to 2.4835 GHz and runs Bluetooth Low Energy 4.2, IEEE 802.15.4 (O-QPSK) and generic FSK/GFSK at 250, 500 and 1000 kbps through one single-ended antenna pin with an on-chip balun. An on-chip DC-DC converter lets it run from 0.9 V to 1.795 V (boost, one alkaline cell), 2.1 V to 4.2 V (buck, coin cell) or 1.71 V to 3.6 V with the converter bypassed. The KW41Z, KW31Z and KW21Z differ in which radio protocols they carry.

operation.text: Six parts come in one 48-pin 7 x 7 mm laminate QFN: KW41Z runs Bluetooth Low Energy, IEEE 802.15.4 and generic FSK; KW31Z runs Bluetooth Low Energy and generic FSK; KW21Z runs IEEE 802.15.4. Each comes with 512 KB flash and 128 KB SRAM or 256 KB flash and 64 KB SRAM.

The transceiver is direct-conversion on receive and constant-envelope on transmit, with a PLL tuning 2.36 GHz to 2.483 GHz and locking in under 25 µs. It can sit on any channel frequency from 2.36 GHz to 2.487 GHz. BLE runs 1 Mbps GFSK with up to two simultaneous hardware connections in any master/slave combination; IEEE 802.15.4-2011 runs 250 kbps O-QPSK (2000 kchip/s, 62.5 ksym/s) with dual-PAN address matching and antenna diversity; generic FSK runs 250, 500 or 1000 kbps with GFSK (BT 0.3, 0.5, 0.7; h 0.32, 0.5, 0.7) or MSK. Link-layer and packet processing for each standard are in hardware. NXP offers certified BLE and IEEE 802.15.4 protocol stacks for the part, Thread among them, with BLE application profiles.

Zero-IF receiver: the RF front end mixes the signal straight to baseband, where it is filtered, amplified and converted to digital; the samples are decimated, demodulated and handed to the packet or link-layer hardware.

Once a channel is chosen the fractional-N PLL tunes coarse then fine until it locks; the modulated signal is buffered into a multi-stage PA. The PA output (RF_P, RF_N) is differential and an on-chip balun turns it into the single-ended ANT port, which receive shares through an internal switch. Output power is set in PA_POWER[5:0] from -30 dBm to 3.5 dBm. External PA and LNA stages are supported through the ANT_A, ANT_B, TX_SWITCH and RX_SWITCH front-end controls.
Harmonic levels are quoted with the recommended two-component match on the antenna port and depend on the tolerance and Q of those two parts. Maximum RF input power is 10 dBm.

BLE and generic FSK work from a 26 MHz or 32 MHz crystal; IEEE 802.15.4 needs 32 MHz. The radio is designed for ±20 ppm total frequency error over life, covering temperature, mechanical stress and aging; ±40 ppm over operating conditions meets IEEE 802.15.4. Load capacitance of 7 pF to 13 pF is integrated on the die and programmable. The crystal drive level limit is 200 µW and its ESR 60 Ω at most. The oscillator clock can be sent out on XTAL_OUT, enabled by XTAL_OUT_EN (PTB0 or PTC6). The MCU can run from this oscillator or from the FLL.

A 32 kHz or 32.768 kHz crystal on EXTAL32K/XTAL32K (PTB16, PTB17) keeps Bluetooth timing accurate through low-power modes and clocks the RTC; enabled, it adds about 1.3 µA to 1.9 µA at 25 °C depending on the mode.

The multipurpose clock generator has a slow internal reference trimmable from 31.25 kHz to 39.0625 kHz (2% across temperature), a fast 4 MHz internal reference (5% across temperature) and an FLL that makes 20 MHz to 48 MHz from either an internal or external reference. A 1 kHz low-power oscillator (LPO) is one clock choice for the COP watchdog and the LPTMR. Core and system clocks reach 48 MHz, bus and flash 24 MHz; in VLPR and VLPS the core is limited to 4 MHz and bus and flash to 1 MHz.

Arm Cortex-M0+ with a two-stage pipeline, Thumb instruction set, NVIC with 32 vectored interrupts at four priority levels plus one non-maskable interrupt, and a wake-up interrupt controller that takes over from the NVIC in very deep sleep. Debug is two-wire SWD with two hardware breakpoints, two watchpoints and a micro trace buffer that stores program trace in system RAM. SWD runs to 25 MHz over 1.71 V to 3.6 V. The chip also has a bit-manipulation engine (BME).

Flash is two equal blocks, so code can run from one while the other is erased or programmed. Sectors are 8 KB and can be marked execute-only to keep firmware from being read out. Flash and RAM are protected from debugger access by the security logic, with program and erase protection and access control in the flash controller. Program flash keeps data 5 years minimum after 10 K cycles and 20 years minimum after 1 K cycles; endurance is 10 K cycles minimum.

One inductor serves both outputs: 1.8 V (programmable up to 3 V) on VDD_1P8OUT and 1.5 V on VDD_1P5OUT_PMCIN. DCDC_CFG chooses the topology: tied to VDCDC_IN it is buck (2.1 V to 4.2 V in; needs 2.1 V to start and can then run down to 1.8 V), tied to ground it is boost (0.9 V to 1.795 V in; needs 1.1 V to start). PSWITCH lets outside logic power the chip up and also selects bypass. The converter can run continuous or pulsed; in pulsed (low-power) mode the load must stay under 1 mA. It has its own oscillator for when the reference crystal is not running, reports power-good to the chip as its POR, and provides a scaled battery voltage for the ADC. Start-up typically takes 50 ms and DCDC_STS_DC_OK sets when done. Buck cuts peak receive and transmit current by about 25%, suiting a CR2032 coin cell; boost suits a single AA or AAA alkaline cell over its whole life.

With the converter running, VDD_1P8OUT feeds VDD_0, VDD_1 and VDDA, and VDD_1P5OUT_PMCIN feeds VDD_RF1 and VDD_RF2; VDD_XTAL can take either rail. The 1.5 V rail is for the chip alone; it should be programmed (DCDC_VDD1P5CTRL_TRG_BUCK or _BOOST) to stay at 1.425 V or more for reliable radio work. The 1.8 V rail can also feed external parts: in buck, up to 44 mA at 1.8 V or 31.4 mA at 3.0 V with the MCU running and the radio on; 38.9 mA at 1.8 V and 20.9 mA at 3.0 V from a 3.0 V input with the MCU running and other peripherals off. Total converter output is at most 125 mW, including the chip's own draw. With the converter bypassed, VDD_RF1, VDD_RF2, VDD_XTAL and VDD_1P5OUT_PMCIN accept 1.5 V to 3.6 V (radio supplies 1.425 V minimum) and VDD_0, VDD_1, VDDA and VDCDC_IN 1.71 V to 3.6 V. An external inductor is needed only for buck or boost.

The PMC provides power-on reset, a low-voltage detector with selectable trip points and reset (brown-out) capability, a programmable low-voltage warning interrupt, a buffered bandgap reference and factory trim of bandgap and LVD. Peripheral clocks can be gated off one by one. The radio can hold its state while the core sits in a stop mode, so it is ready to communicate soon after waking.

Run, Wait and Stop each have a very-low-power variant (VLPR, VLPW, VLPS); WFI enters Wait or Stop according to the Cortex-M0+ SLEEPDEEP bit. Below them sit the low-leakage modes LLS3, LLS2 and VLLS3 to VLLS0. I/O states are held in every mode. Radio sea-of-gates logic keeps its state through LLSx, VLLS3 and VLLS2, where the BLE, 802.15.4 and FSK deep-sleep logic can run from the 32 kHz clock; in VLLS1 and VLLS0 the radio is power-gated and its state lost. VLLS0 is not available with the converter in buck or boost. Radio operation in VLPR needs the converter in continuous mode.

From VDD reaching 1.8 V to the first instruction takes at most 300 µs (normal boot). In bypass that limit is not met when VDD_1P5 < 1.6 V at 25 °C or 1.5 V ≤ VDD_1P5 ≤ 1.8 V, nor, with VDD_1P5 tied to VDD_1P8, when the supply slews at 100 V/s or less. RESET_b (PTA2 by default) is bidirectional with an internal pull-down only; an external reset pulse must be at least 100 ns. The falling POR threshold is 0.8 V to 1.5 V. RAM is retained down to VDD = 1.2 V.

All inputs have hysteresis and an optional pull-up (20 kΩ to 50 kΩ); every GPIO can raise an interrupt or a wake-up. PTB0, PTB1, PTC1 to PTC3, PTC6, PTC7, PTC17 and PTC18 can switch to high drive, specified at 20 mA from 2.7 V to 3.6 V; the rest have normal drive only, specified at 5 mA. Total current out of or into all ports is limited to 100 mA each way. The pins clamp to VSS through an ESD diode and have no diode to VDD; the input limit is VDD + 0.3 V (PTC0 to PTC3 included). The 48-pin package has 26 digital pins, usable as GPIO or for LPUART, SPI, I2C, ADC, timers and the other muxed functions, and GPIO can form an interrupt-driven keyboard matrix.

Four DMA channels with dual-address transfers, programmable source, destination and size, 32-byte transfer control descriptors in local memory, nested minor and major loops, channel linking, scatter/gather, and fixed or round-robin arbitration. Each channel starts by software, by linking or by a peripheral request routed through the DMA multiplexer, which also offers two periodic triggers.

TPM0 has four channels, TPM1 and TPM2 two each: 16-bit counters with input capture, output compare and edge- or centre-aligned PWM, hardware triggers, a shared global time base, and quadrature decoding on TPM1 and TPM2. The PIT has two 32-bit interrupt timers that can trigger the ADC. The LPTMR is a 16-bit timer or pulse counter that works in every power mode. The RTC has a 32-bit seconds counter and alarm, a compensated 16-bit prescaler, write locks, and can wake the chip. The carrier modulator timer (CMT) drives CMT_IRO in time, baseband or FSK modes or directly from software. The COP watchdog runs from the LPO or bus clock.

Two SPI modules (master or slave, up to 12 MHz master and 6 MHz slave, DMA-capable); two I2C modules (up to 400 kHz, SMBus 2 features, multi-master, address-match wake-up); one LPUART (13-bit baud divider with fractional divide of 32, 8- or 9-bit data, RTS/CTS flow control, DMA, works in Stop and VLPS).

16-bit successive-approximation ADC: differential 16, 13, 11 and 9-bit modes, single-ended 16, 12, 10 and 8-bit modes, up to about 500 ksps at 16 bits without averaging, hardware averaging, compare function, self-calibration, an asynchronous clock for low-noise conversion in low-power modes, and internal channels for temperature and battery voltage. The temperature sensor gives 716 mV at 25 °C with a slope of 1.62 mV/°C. Keep source resistance low; the specifications were measured with under 8 Ω and an RAS × CAS time constant under 1 ns.

The 12-bit DAC (output DAC0_OUT on PTB18) converts in 1 µs at high speed or 2 µs at low speed, can generate square, triangle and sawtooth waves on its own, and drives at most 100 pF and 1 mA; a 47 pF load can improve its bandwidth. The comparator has a 6-bit DAC reference, up to eight inputs, selectable hysteresis and edge interrupts, a fast or a low-power mode, and works in every mode except VLLS0. The VREF block gives 1.2 V (1.1950 V typ) trimmable in 0.5 mV steps; when VREF_OUT is used as a reference it needs a 100 nF capacitor on the pin.

The TSI reads up to 16 electrodes in every power mode, with 16-bit results, compensation for temperature and supply drift, software or hardware triggers, up to 4096 scans, DMA, and wake-up from low-power modes.

An AES-128 accelerator handles ECB, CBC and CTR (plus DES modes), CMAC, XCBC-MAC, CCM and GCM. A true random number generator supplies 512 bits of entropy at a time for a software DRBG. Each chip carries an 80-bit unique ID and a 40-bit MAC address from which a 48-bit BLE or 64-bit IEEE 802.15.4 address can be built. BLE 4.2 secure connections and IEEE 802.15.4-2011 security are supported.
48-pin laminate QFN, 7 mm x 7 mm, outline document 98ASA00694D. Pins 49 to 64 are ground pads on the underside. Moisture sensitivity level 3; lead-free solder temperature 260 °C maximum.
Switching figures assume 30 pF loads, slew-rate control off and normal drive unless stated.
